title: Procyclicality of US Bank Leverage

scopes.description: Complete assessed workflow for the main Tables 1–8 and the supplied online appendix analyses A–E; appendix companion procedures and inputs remain unresolved.

requirements.description: SNL Financial bank-level quarterly data for the US commercial and savings banks/holding companies selected by the authors, Q1 1994 through Q1 2013, imported as bank_data_raw.xlsx. The workbook must expose period and the 26 SNL variables named in the supplied field dictionary and code: instkey, industry, totassets, taccass, afssec, htmsec, net_lns, gw, cash_equ, totequ, totdep, seniordebt, totsubdebt, rwa, tieroneratio, rwcapitalratio, marketcap, chg_unrealgain, netprofit, gainsaleloan, tot_assetssec, uncmt_onefourrevlin, uncmt_creditcardlin, uncmt_totcommrelin, uncmt_secunderwrit, and uncmt_othcmt.

routes.location: SNL Financial Companies dataset via SNLxl/Excel (current access and terms not established)
routes.description: Authors report a historical SNLxl query using the supplied institution IDs and variable KeyFields, with a US holding-company sample of commercial and savings banks and full coverage depth. The raw bank workbook is not in the supplied package; current access, the later 2015/2016 revisions, exact first-row field names, and full quarter coverage have not been verified. The datasheet also marks its proprietary-data section not applicable, so current rights/access conditions need clarification rather than an inferred barrier.
routes.expected_period: Quarterly Q1 1994 through Q1 2013 for the author-selected US bank holding-company sample; bank data originally downloaded in June 2013 and updated for revisions in October 2015 and June 2016

requirements.description: Quarterly real US GDP levels for Q1 1994 through Q1 2013, prepared as the long-format macro_data_raw.xlsx input. The code imports period and real_gdp, encodes calendar quarters, and computes adjacent-quarter GDP growth; the authors report an October 2015 download vintage.

routes.location: BEA Gross Domestic Product page, quarterly real GDP since 1947; FRED GDPC1 / BEA account A191RX
routes.description: BEA’s official product page links quarterly inflation-adjusted real GDP since 1947 and historical/vintage archives. FRED identifies GDPC1 as BEA account A191RX, quarterly real GDP in chained 2017 dollars at a seasonally adjusted annual rate. These public pages support acquisition of the current quarterly real-GDP level series covering the required Q1 1994–Q1 2013 window, then reformatting to the code’s period and real_gdp workbook fields. Current published values are revised; whether the exact October 2015 author vintage is retrievable and matches the authors’ workbook values remains unverified. The original workbook headers/layout are not supplied, so record the public source-to-target column mapping when preparing the workbook.
routes.expected_period: Quarterly real GDP levels covering Q1 1994 through Q1 2013; author-reported October 2015 vintage is a separate exact-reproduction check.

actions.description: Establish a current permitted route to the author-specified SNL bank data or an author-approved compatible prepared workbook, then populate bank_data_raw.xlsx using the supplied sample-ID list and SNL KeyField mapping.
steps: Confirm current SNL Financial access and the data-use terms for the project; the package does not document a current license or access route.
Use the 932 supplied institution identifiers and the 26 SNL KeyField numbers to request/download the documented US commercial/savings-bank holding-company series with full coverage depth.
Obtain quarterly observations for Q1 1994 through Q1 2013, including the SNLxl period field, and save an Excel workbook named bank_data_raw.xlsx in the configured run directory.

Verify the exported first-row variable names match the supplied do-file’s expected fields before running; preserve the source identifier list separately because the do-file exports to the same filename.
validation: Confirm authorization and permitted data use before acquisition.

Check that the raw workbook exposes all expected fields, includes the author’s full quarterly range and selected institutions, and reflects the documented historical/revision vintage or an author-approved equivalent.
Confirm that the project can retain the data only in accordance with the current SNL terms.

actions.description: Acquire the supported public quarterly BEA real-GDP level series and prepare macro_data_raw.xlsx in the field and history format required by the Stata code, documenting the selected data vintage.
steps: Acquire quarterly real GDP levels from BEA’s “Real GDP (Inflation-Adjusted Dollars): Quarters, Since 1947” product; FRED GDPC1 identifies the corresponding BEA account A191RX as quarterly real GDP in chained 2017 dollars at a seasonally adjusted annual rate. Select the level series, not a percent-change series, and retain the source and vintage metadata.

Check whether the BEA historical/vintage archive can provide the authors’ reported October 2015 vintage. If using the current revised series, record the retrieval date and vintage and do not describe it as an exact historical-value match.

Reshape/reformat the quarterly observations for Q1 1994 through Q1 2013 into a long-format workbook with period and real_gdp columns, documenting the source-column mapping and quarter encoding; save it as macro_data_raw.xlsx in the configured run directory.
validation: Confirm one correctly ordered observation per quarter from Q1 1994 through Q1 2013 and that the selected data are real-GDP levels, not growth rates.
Check the source-to-target column mapping, units, quarterly frequency, seasonal-adjustment/annual-rate metadata, and selected vintage; record any difference from the authors’ October 2015 vintage.
After authorized preparation, verify the code creates gdp_data.dta before the bank merge and inspect the resulting quarter alignment.

review_notes: The initial partial draft was saved after source reading and before environment/catalog/resource checks.

The supplied identifier file contains 932 unique numeric bank identifiers, and the workbook inspection returns 26 named SNL KeyField mappings plus the separate real_gdp entry. Neither file contains the quarterly bank/GDP observations required by the code.
The do-file creates gdp_data.dta from macro_data_raw.xlsx before importing and merging the SNL bank workbook. The frozen checklist’s two read dependencies are both reviewed as mandatory inputs.
The author code’s explicit winsor, eststo, estpost, and esttab commands are available in the checked Stata 18 environment. No author code or dataset was executed.

The bounded frozen-catalog lookups did not identify a matching local candidate; the default local PostgreSQL endpoint did not respond. Neither check establishes data absence, licensing, or the status of other configured sources.

The official BEA product page and FRED’s BEA-sourced GDPC1 series page support public acquisition of quarterly real-GDP levels spanning the required period. Current product series, frequency, units, and seasonality are identified; the exact author-reported October 2015 values and workbook headers/layout remain a separate vintage/format check. No data were downloaded.

The full-pipeline target retains the supplied online appendix A–E analyses. Their companion workflow and compatible inputs remain unresolved; the proposal requests those materials without treating appendix analyses as optional or truncating the target.
